sentences.text: In this appeal, the petitioner is seeking enhancement of compensation.
2. For the sake of convenience, the parties shall be referred to as per their status before the Tribunal.

3. The undisputed facts is that, on 26.08.2012 at about 11.30 a.m., there was an accident between Scorpio car bearing Reg.No.KA-03/MD-7931 in which the petitioner was the inmate, and a Tanker lorry bearing No.KA-19/AC-4800 in front of IMA office at NH-26, Kadur-Birur Road, injuring the petitioner.
After taking treatment, the petitioner approached the Tribunal for grant of compensation of Rs.10,00,000/-.
The claim was opposed by the Insurance Company.

After taking the evidence and hearing both parties, the Tribunal by impugned judgment awarded compensation of Rs.48,574/-
with 6% interest p.a., NC: 2024:KHC:32700 Pleading inadequacy and seeking enhancement of compensation, the petitioner is before this Court.

4. Heard the arguments of Sri.S.G.Chakrapani, learned counsel for the petitioner and Sri.H.S.Lingaraju, learned counsel for the Insurance Company.
5.
It is contended by the learned counsel for the petitioner that in an accident, the petitioner has suffered fracture of left Zygomatic complex with medially displaced Zygomatic arch.
He was under hospitalization for four days, which warrants incidental expenses.
The Tribunal did not consider loss of amenities and discomfort.
The compensation awarded towards pain and suffering and other heads is on the lower side, and sought for enhancement.

6. Per contra, the learned Counsel for the Insurance Company has contended that the Tribunal considered the totality of the injuries and awarded just compensation and it is not a case for enhancement.
I have given my anxious consideration to the arguments addressed on behalf of both sides and also perused the materials on record.

sentences.text: The compensation awarded by the Tribunal has been satisfied by the Insurance Company.

Hence,
there is no need to go in detail about the accident and entitlement of the petitioner to get compensation.
The issue in this appeal is regarding quantum of compensation.
9. The Tribunal has awarded Rs.15,000/- towards pain and suffering, Rs.28,041/- towards medical expenses, Rs.533/- towards loss of earning during laid- up and Rs.5,000/- towards incidental expenses.
10. The medical certificate and also the discharge summary clearly point out the fracture sustained by the petitioner to his left zygomatic complex with medially displaced zygomatic arch.
Such an injury may not affect future earning but it will certainly cause pain and suffering and loss of amenities and NC: 2024:KHC:32700 discomfort.
The petitioner was under hospitalization for four days at Government Hospital, Kadur and also at Hemavathi Hospital, Hassan.
The accident is of the year 2012.

Towards pain and suffering, a sum of Rs.30,000/-; medical expenses of Rs.28,041/-,
incidental expenses of Rs.5,000/-, loss of amenities and discomfort at Rs.25,000/- and the loss of income during laid-up of three months at the rate of Rs.7,000/- per month comes to Rs.21,000/-.
Total compensation comes to Rs.1,09,041/- as against Rs.48,574/- assessed by the Tribunal, thereby enhancement of Rs.60,467/- rounded off to Rs.60,500/-.
It is the just compensation that the petitioner is entitled to, in the facts and circumstances of the case.
